repairTwo.mechanismVerifiedNotAssumed: Read off the pinned source rather than carried over from another family. All 13 are /Ch choosers this packet deliberately leaves unmade. Each ships its own /AP /N drawing white fill and ONE BOTTOM RULE - '1 g 0 0 84.1091 15.1201 re f 0 G 0 0.5 m 84.1091 0.5 l s' - and each declares /MK /BC [0 0 0] with /BS /S /U, the ISO 32000-1 Table 166 style meaning a single line along the bottom of the rectangle. The unwritten-input drop cleared that appearance, updateFieldAppearances regenerated one from /MK /BC alone because pdf-lib's provider never reads /BS, and flatten() stamped a closed four-sided box where the issuer prints a rule.
repairTwo.thisIsNotTheIllinoisMechanism: Measured, not assumed. Unlike ca-17b-reduction-set in this same return, JDF 417's widgets DO ship a usable appearance; nothing here is a missing /Off state. The two families in this lane fail the same obligation through two different mechanisms and take two different repairs.
repairTwo.whatWasFoundBeyondTheThirteen: After the first flag the delivered bytes still carried 10 four-sided boxes - 9 on page 1 and 1 on page 3 - at County, the defendant name, Case Number, 1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 1.6, the street address and the city. suppressSynthesizedWidgetBorders covers only UNWRITTEN fields by design; these are the caption fields the packet writes the participant's own details into. Every one declares /BS /S /U and ships a bottom-rule-only appearance, so they are the same defect and the same obligation, and the Colorado Judicial Department's writing rule was being delivered as a box drawn around the participant's own name, county and case number. Because that ink sits inside a declared write box, no completeness counter and no raster receipt can see it. They were repaired too, under the same obligation, with honorWidgetBorderStyle.
